habitat: Pairs or small flocks in towns, scavenging and associating with cattle and wild ungulates. Large noisy flocks gather to roost.
summary: A very common or abundant resident. The head, mantle and breast are black, the rest is brown and darker above, the vent is white, and the wings are black and white. The bill, facial skin and legs are yellow. Nape plumes have a greenish iridescence. The immature has duller facial skin. It chatters, clucks and squeaks. Newman marks it as an introduced species. No Kemp estimate is stored.

head.pattern: Head black. Yellow facial skin. Nape plumes have a greenish iridescence.

upperparts.pattern: Mantle black. The rest is brown, darker above.

underparts.pattern: Vent white. The body otherwise brown.

wings.pattern: Black and white. Large white wing-patches are conspicuous in flight.

viewNotes.note: Black head and breast, brown body, yellow bill and legs.
Yellow facial skin and a white vent.
Nape plumes with a greenish iridescence.
The underwing is not given a separate colour.

calls.description: A variety of chattering calls, clucks, squeaks and melodious phrases. The grade A call is from near Orkney. The filename is XC533469-1 Myna.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a very common or abundant resident and marks it introduced. Avibase also lists it as introduced, not as rare or accidental, so all twelve months are listed. Greenish iridescence is not stored as a plumage colour. The grade A call is from North West. No Kemp estimate is stored.

population.notes: No sourced Kruger estimate is currently available; taxonomy or later records require separate research.
